rules.sentence: Gram staining is often the initial diagnostic test for evaluating infections due to its ability to quickly identify the presence and type of bacteria.

However, although Gram staining offers quick insights, it is less specific compared to advanced molecular techniques and genetic sequencing, which can precisely identify bacterial species and resistance patterns, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and treatment efficacy.[17]
Gram-negative bacteria (GNB) are among the world's most significant public health problems due to their high resistance to antibiotics.

These microorganisms have significant clinical importance in hospitals because they often require patients to be in the intensive care unit (ICU), and patients are at high risk of morbidity and mortality.
